info.title: Ambivo Third-Party Integrations API
info.description:
Third-party integration endpoints for PayPal, SparkApt, GitHub, Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive.

## Authentication
All `/user/*` and `/github/*` endpoints require a Bearer JWT token in the `Authorization` header.
The PayPal webhook endpoint (`/paypal/webhook/connect`) is public (called by PayPal's servers).

## Response Pattern
- **Success**: `{ "result": 1, ...data }`
- **Error**: `{ "result": 2, "error": "message" }`

## Integration Overview

| Integration | Model | Endpoints | Auth |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PayPal** | Webhook receiver + admin management | 2 routes | Webhook: none (public); Management: JWT + tenant admin |
| **SparkApt** | Automation-action + setup management | 1 route | Setup: JWT + tenant admin; Sync: via automation rules engine |
| **GitHub** | Token vault + Issues proxy | 2 routes (full CRUD) | JWT + module privilege `github_token` |
| **Google Drive** | OAuth connect + file read | 6 routes | JWT; callback is public |
| **Microsoft OneDrive** | OAuth connect + file read | 5 routes | JWT; callback is public |

### Cloud Drive Connect

Google Drive and OneDrive share one route shape: build a consent URL, let the provider call
back, then list and download files against the stored connection.

Both use the OAuth 2.0 **Authorization Code Flow as a confidential client** — the provider
redirects with a short-lived code, and the code-for-token exchange happens server to server
using a client secret that never reaches the browser. No access token is ever minted in or
exposed to the front end. The two `/auth/callback` routes are therefore the only unauthenticated
endpoints here, because the provider's redirect carries no Bearer token.

A user may connect **several accounts per provider**. Each is addressed by its `email`, which
the file, download and refresh endpoints take to select a connection.

One asymmetry to be aware of: `DELETE /gdrive/auth/status` disconnects a Google Drive account,
and OneDrive has no equivalent.

### SparkApt Integration

SparkApt sync operates as an automation action (`sync_to_sparkapt`) within the
automation rules engine. API key configuration is managed via a dedicated setup endpoint.

**Trigger**: An automation rule fires on contact `create` or `update` events.

**Two sync modes** (controlled by `mode` arg):
- `client` (default) — pushes contact to SparkApt's **Clients** tab via `createClient` GraphQL mutation
- `inquiry` — pushes contact to SparkApt's **Leads** tab via `createClientInquiry` GraphQL mutation. Agent converts to client in Spark UI.

**Automation rule action entry** (add to `action_list` array):
```json
{
  "action": "sync_to_sparkapt",
  "filter": "",
  "update": [],
  "level": "user",
  "args_payload": {
    "mode": "inquiry",
    "url_name": "joseph-pineda"
  },
  "match_criteria_dict": {},
  "data_level": "single",
  "initial_delay": "0"
}
```

**Full automation rule example** (contact create → add to campaign + sync to SparkAPT):
```json
{
  "entity_type": "contact",
  "event_name": "create",
  "is_active": true,
  "action_list": [
    {
      "action": "add_to_campaign",
      "filter": "",
      "update": [],
      "level": "user",
      "args_payload": {
        "userid": "5b23c83842e02e5b677d34dc",
        "campaign_id": "679a9c0c40ff620c52865427",
        "first_name": "{{ name }}",
        "last_name": "{{ name }}",
        "email": "{{ email }}",
        "phone": "{{ phone }}"
      },
      "match_criteria_dict": {
        "userid": "5b23c83842e02e5b677d34dc"
      },
      "data_level": "single",
      "initial_delay": "0"
    },
    {
      "action": "sync_to_sparkapt",
      "filter": "",
      "update": [],
      "level": "user",
      "args_payload": {
        "mode": "inquiry",
        "url_name": "joseph-pineda"
      },
      "match_criteria_dict": {},
      "data_level": "single",
      "initial_delay": "0"
    }
  ],
  "tenant_id": "5a77b0fb8b57864d7e16d4ba"
}
```

**Key differences from other actions**: The `sync_to_sparkapt` action does **not** need
template variables like `{{ email }}` — all contact fields are auto-mapped from the
trigger payload. Only use `args_payload` for mode selection and overrides.

**`args_payload` fields** (all optional — set in the action's `args_payload` dict):

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `"client"` or `"inquiry"` | `"client"` | Push to Clients tab or Leads tab |
| `url_name` | string | `"joseph-pineda"` | Agent URL identifier (inquiry mode only) |
| `budget` | string | — | Override budget |
| `notes` | string | — | Override notes |
| `leadSource` | string | `"Ambivo CRM"` | Override lead source |
| `moveInDate` | string | — | Override move-in date |
| `currentStatus` | string | — | Override SparkAPT status |

**Validation rules**: Sync requires at least `firstName` or `lastName`, **and** at least
`email` or `phone`. Missing either condition returns `{"result": 2, "error": "..."}` without
calling SparkApt.

**Field mapping** (Ambivo contact → SparkApt):

| Ambivo Field | SparkApt Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `first_name` | `firstName` | Required (at least one of name fields) |
| `last_name` | `lastName` | Required (at least one of name fields) |
| `email_list[0].email` | `email` | Required (email or phone) |
| `email_list[1].email` | `secondaryEmail` | Optional |
| `phone_list[0].phone` | `phone` | Required (email or phone) |
| `estimated_budget` | `budget` | String |
| `source` | `leadSource` | Default: `"Ambivo CRM"` |
| `description` + latest `comments[-1].comment` | `notes` | Pipe-separated (`" | "`) |
| `match_preferences_dict.movein_date` | `moveInDate` | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `match_preferences_dict.min_rent` | `minRent` | Integer |
| `match_preferences_dict.max_rent` | `maxRent` | Integer |
| `match_preferences_dict.bedrooms` | `bedroom` | List of UnitType |
| `match_preferences_dict.bathrooms` | `bathroom` | Float |
| `match_preferences_dict.pet_type` | `petType` | String |
| `match_preferences_dict.pet_count` | `petNumber` | Integer |
| `status` | `currentStatus` | Mapped via status table (see below) |
| — | `isPercentBuildingCommission` | Always `False` |

**Status mapping** (Ambivo → SparkApt):
```
open/assigned/attempted → lead
contacted              → follow_up
meeting-setup          → scheduling_tours
customer               → signed_lease
lost/lost-followup     → lost
inactive               → backlog
incorrect/disqualified → lost
```

**Additional integration patterns**:

- **Direct service usage** (outside automation): Instantiate `SparkAPTService` directly for ad-hoc syncs:
  ```python
  from omnilonely.service.sparkapt_service import SparkAPTService
  svc = SparkAPTService(application, user=user, tenant=tenant)
  result = svc.sync_contact_to_sparkapt(contact.toJSON(application), action_args={"mode": "client"})
  ```
- **Direct client usage** (low-level): Use `SparkAPTClient` directly for queries or non-contact operations:
  ```python
  from omnilonely.service.sparkapt import SparkAPTClient
  client = SparkAPTClient(api_key="...")
  props = client.get_properties(city_id=1013, min_rent=1500, max_rent=2500)
  ```
- **Syncing back**: Poll `get_clients()` or `get_client(id)` to read status changes (e.g., `signed_lease`, `moved_in`) and sync back to Ambivo.
- **Property search**: `get_properties(city_id, min_rent, max_rent, bedroom)` can power apartment recommendations within Ambivo.
- **API key management**: Per-tenant keys stored in `sparkapt_setup` collection, cached in Redis (4h TTL).
  Managed via `POST /user/admin/tenant/sparkapt/setup`. Falls back to config then hardcoded default.
  Resolution order: Redis cache → MongoDB `sparkapt_setup` → `config.config_data["sparkapt_api_key"]` → hardcoded.
- **Multi-agent limitation**: Currently all data goes to one agent's account. For per-agent routing, each agent needs their own API key.

**Service files**:
- `src/omnilonely/service/sparkapt_service.py` — `SparkAPTService.sync_contact_to_sparkapt()`
- `src/omnilonely/service/sparkapt/sparkapt_client.py` — GraphQL client (queries + mutations)
- `src/omnilonely/web/sparkapt_endpoints.py` — Setup CRUD endpoint
- API endpoint: `POST https://api.sparkapt.com` with header `Spark-Api-Key`

post.summary: Receive PayPal webhook or IPN event
post.description:
Public endpoint that PayPal calls when a payment event occurs.
No authentication — PayPal sends the event payload directly.

**Supports two formats**:
- **Webhooks API** (`application/json`) — standard PayPal webhook events with `id`, `event_type`, `resource`
- **IPN** (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) — legacy Instant Payment Notifications with flat fields like `mc_gross`, `payer_email`, `txn_id`

IPN is auto-detected by the presence of `txn_id` or `txn_type` in the parsed form body.

**Rate limited**: 10 requests / 60 seconds per IP.

---

## PayPal Setup Instructions

### Option A: Webhooks API (Recommended)

1. **Create a webhook account** in Ambivo via `POST /user/admin/tenant/paypal_connect/manage`
   with `action: "create"`. Copy the returned `webhook_url`.
2. Go to **[PayPal Developer Dashboard](https://developer.paypal.com/dashboard/applications)** →
   select your app → **Webhooks** → **Add Webhook**.
3. Paste the full URL: `https://goferapi.ambivo.com/paypal/webhook/connect?account_id=<your_account_id>`
4. Select the events you want to receive (e.g. `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED`,
   `PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED`, `CHECKOUT.ORDER.COMPLETED`).
5. **Save** — PayPal will show a **Webhook ID**. Copy it.
6. **(Optional but recommended)** Update the Ambivo account with credentials for signature
   verification: `action: "update"` with `paypal_client_id`, `paypal_client_secret`,
   `paypal_webhook_id`, and `paypal_mode` (`sandbox` or `live`).

### Option B: IPN (Instant Payment Notifications)

1. **Create a webhook account** in Ambivo (same as above). Copy the `account_id`.
2. Go to **[PayPal IPN Settings](https://www.paypal.com/cgi-bin/customerprofileweb?cmd=_display-ipn-pref)**
   (or PayPal account → **Settings** → **Notifications** → **Instant payment notifications**).
3. Click **Choose IPN Settings** (or **Update**).
4. Set the **Notification URL** to:
   `https://goferapi.ambivo.com/paypal/webhook/connect?account_id=<your_account_id>`
5. Select **Receive IPN messages (Enabled)** → **Save**.
6. PayPal will now POST `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` data to your endpoint for every
   payment event.

**Note**: You can use both Webhooks API and IPN simultaneously on the same account — they use
different dedup keys (`id` vs `txn_id`) so there are no conflicts.

---

## Processing Flow

1. Parse body — try JSON first, fall back to form-urlencoded (IPN)
2. Validate `account_id` query parameter
3. Look up PayPal Connect account (must be active)
4. Soft-validate source IP against PayPal CIDR ranges
5. Verify webhook signature (Webhooks API only, soft-fail). Skipped for IPN.
6. Deduplicate — by event `id` (Webhooks API) or `txn_id` (IPN)
7. Normalize event type — IPN: synthesize from `payment_status` (e.g. `IPN.PAYMENT.COMPLETED`)
8. Enrich payload with Ambivo metadata (`ambivo_ts`, `ambivo_tenant_id`, `ambivo_sig_verified`, `ambivo_source`, etc.)
9. Store in `paypal_webhook_events_log` collection
10. Fire automation rules (non-blocking) for payment event types:
    - `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED`
    - `PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED`
    - `CHECKOUT.ORDER.COMPLETED`
    - `BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.ACTIVATED`
    - `IPN.PAYMENT.COMPLETED`

## IPN Details

**IPN event type mapping** (`payment_status` → `event_type`):
- `Completed` → `IPN.PAYMENT.COMPLETED`
- `Refunded` → `IPN.PAYMENT.REFUNDED`
- `Pending` → `IPN.PAYMENT.PENDING`
- Other → `IPN.{PAYMENT_STATUS}`

**IPN field mapping for payment processing**:

| IPN Field | Maps To |
|---|---|
| `mc_gross` | amount |
| `payer_email` | email |
| `first_name` + `last_name` | name |
| `txn_id` | reference_number, source_id |
| `receipt_id` | appended to reference_number |
| `item_name1` / `item_name` | description |
| `payment_date` | payment_date (timezone stripped, parsed) |
| `mc_currency` | currency |

**Real-world IPN example** (actual PayPal IPN from IP `173.0.81.140`, which is in CIDR `173.0.80.0/20`):
```
curl -X POST 'https://goferapi.ambivo.com/paypal/webhook/connect?account_id=be2bfbd0290644efa0b276723ed021d1' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d 'mc_gross=1.00&protection_eligibility=Eligible&address_status=confirmed\
&payer_id=U7TQLLV3JJPAY&tax=0.00&address_street=64+Rosewood+Ln\
&payment_date=19%3A33%3A04+Mar+06%2C+2026+PST&payment_status=Completed\
&charset=windows-1252&address_zip=94506&first_name=Hemant&mc_fee=0.52\
&address_country_code=US&notify_version=3.9&payer_status=unverified\
&business=sgosain%40ambivo.com&num_cart_items=1&address_city=Danville\
&payer_email=sunny%40nashapartments.com&txn_id=2JM05574442162101\
&payment_type=instant&last_name=Gosain&address_state=CA\
&item_name1=Donate&receiver_email=sgosain%40ambivo.com\
&payment_fee=0.52&quantity1=1&receiver_id=U5AMEA4VVJ68N\
&txn_type=cart&mc_gross_1=1.00&mc_currency=USD&residence_country=US\
&receipt_id=3933-2686-2831-3099&transaction_subject=Donate+Here\
&payment_gross=1.00&ipn_track_id=000000000000000079319f0c047e656d'
```

This would be stored as:
- `event_type`: `IPN.PAYMENT.COMPLETED`
- `id`: `2JM05574442162101` (from `txn_id`)
- `ambivo_source`: `ipn`
- `ambivo_ip_is_paypal`: `true` (173.0.81.140 is in 173.0.80.0/20)
- `ambivo_sig_verified`: `true` (signature verification skipped for IPN)

---

## Automation Rules Integration

After storing a payment event, the system fires automation rules **non-blocking** via
`AutomationRulesService.evaluate_automation_rules()` with:

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `entity_type` | `paypal_webhook` |
| `event_name` | `payment_received` |
| `instance_payload` | Full stored event doc (all PayPal fields + Ambivo enrichment) |

**Trigger event types**: `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED`, `PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED`,
`CHECKOUT.ORDER.COMPLETED`, `BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.ACTIVATED`, `IPN.PAYMENT.COMPLETED`.

**To enable downstream processing**, the tenant must configure an automation rule:
```json
{
  "entity_type": "paypal_webhook",
  "event_name": "payment_received",
  "is_active": true,
  "action_list": [
    {
      "action": "process_payment",
      "args_payload": {},
      "match_criteria_dict": {},
      "data_level": "single",
      "initial_delay": "0"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Available actions** for `paypal_webhook` / `payment_received` rules:
- `process_payment` — creates contact (if needed) + invoice + payment record
- `add_to_campaign` — adds payer to a drip/email campaign
- `sync_to_sparkapt` — syncs contact data to SparkAPT
- `send_notification` — sends alert to tenant admin

**Important**: Payment processing (contact + invoice + payment creation) is **not automatic**.
It only happens if:
1. An automation rule with `action: "process_payment"` is configured, **OR**
2. A tenant admin manually calls `action: "process_payment"` on the management endpoint
   with the stored `event_id`.

Without an automation rule, events are **stored only** — no contact/invoice/payment records are created.

---

**PayPal IP CIDR ranges** (for soft validation):
`64.4.240.0/21`, `64.4.248.0/22`, `66.211.168.0/22`, `91.243.72.0/23`,
`173.0.80.0/20`, `185.177.52.0/22`, `192.160.215.0/24`, `198.54.216.0/23`

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: Identifies which tenant's PayPal Connect account receives the event

resource.description: Event resource data (payment details, payer info, etc.)

schema.description:
PayPal IPN (Instant Payment Notification) payload.
All fields are flat key-value pairs. Detected by presence of `txn_id` or `txn_type`.
PayPal sends this from IPs in the `173.0.80.0/20` range (among others).

payment_status.description: Payment status — drives event_type synthesis (Completed, Pending, Refunded, Reversed, etc.)

receipt_id.description: PayPal receipt ID (appended to reference_number in payment processing)

payment_date.description: Payment date in PayPal format (e.g. '19:33:04 Mar 06, 2026 PST')

400.description: Bad request (missing account_id, invalid JSON, or unrecognized body format)

invalid_body.summary: Body is neither valid JSON nor IPN

value.message: Invalid body: not JSON or IPN

post.description:
Multi-action admin endpoint for PayPal Connect webhook account management.
Dispatch via the `action` field in the request body.

**Requires**: JWT + tenant admin role.

**Available actions**:
- `create` — Create a new webhook account (returns `webhook_url` to configure in PayPal).
  Optionally accepts `paypal_client_id`, `paypal_client_secret`, `paypal_webhook_id`,
  `paypal_mode` for webhook signature verification.
- `list` — List all webhook accounts for the tenant (credentials masked)
- `update` — Update label, description, active status, or credentials
- `delete` — Soft-delete (deactivate) or hard-delete an account
- `get_events` — Retrieve paginated stored webhook events
- `process_payment` — Process a webhook event into contact + invoice + payment

**Webhook signature verification**: When `paypal_client_id`, `paypal_client_secret`, and
`paypal_webhook_id` are configured on an account, inbound webhooks are verified against
PayPal's `/v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature` API. Verification is **soft-fail** —
events are always stored, but `ambivo_sig_verified: false` is recorded on failed events.
`paypal_mode` controls sandbox vs production API URL.

delete_soft.summary: Account deactivated (soft delete — returns full account)

post.description:
CRUD management for per-tenant SparkAPT API key stored in the `sparkapt_setup`
MongoDB collection. The API key is used by the automation engine when syncing
contacts to SparkAPT.

**Requires**: JWT + tenant admin role.

**Available actions**:
- `get` — Retrieve the current setup (API key masked in response)
- `upsert` — Create or update the setup (requires `api_key`)
- `delete` — Remove the setup (falls back to config/hardcoded key)

**Caching**: API keys are cached in Redis for 4 hours (`sparkapt_api_key_{tenant_id}`).
The `upsert` action immediately updates the cache. The `delete` action invalidates it.

**Key resolution order** (used by `SparkAPTService._get_api_key_async()`):
1. Redis cache (4h TTL)
2. `sparkapt_setup` collection (find_one by tenant_id)
3. `config.config_data["sparkapt_api_key"]`
4. Hardcoded fallback

get.summary: Build the Google Drive consent URL
get.description:
Returns the Google consent URL the browser should be sent to in order to connect a
Google Drive account. Nothing is stored at this point — the connection is only
persisted once the provider calls back.

The `state` round-tripped through Google carries the calling user and tenant, plus the
optional navigation hints below, so the callback knows which account to attach the
credential to and where to send the browser afterwards.

Scope requested includes `drive.file`. A connect that returns without it will still
complete, but file listing will be empty.

parameters.name: post_navigation
parameters.description: Where to send the browser immediately after a successful callback.

parameters.name: final_navigation
parameters.description: Final destination once post-connect setup finishes.

auth_url.description: Send the browser here to begin consent.

get.summary: OAuth callback — exchanges the authorization code
get.description:
**Called by Google, not by your application.** This endpoint is unauthenticated by
necessity: the provider redirects the browser here and no Bearer token is present on
that navigation.

It exchanges the authorization code for tokens server to server, then stores the
resulting refresh token against the user and tenant named in `state`. The client
secret used for the exchange never leaves the server.

Register this path as an authorized redirect URI with the provider. It is not intended
to be called directly.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Short-lived authorization code issued by Google.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque value round-tripped from the authorization request.

200.description: Envelope reporting whether the connection was stored. `result` is 2 when the code exchange fails or the provider returns no refresh token — the most common cause of the latter is re-consenting an account that is already connected.

get.description:
Lists every Google Drive account the caller has connected in this tenant. One user may
connect several accounts; each is returned as its own entry keyed by `email`, and that
`email` is what the file and download endpoints expect.

Each entry carries `reauthorization_needed`. It is set by actually attempting a token
refresh against Google, so it reflects the live state of the grant rather than a stored
flag — a connection whose access was revoked provider-side reports `true` here.

200.description: Connected drives, each with its live reauthorization state.

delete.description:
Removes a stored Google Drive connection. Requires the `gdrive` module delete privilege.

This drops the credential held by Ambivo; it does not revoke the grant at Google. A user
who wants the grant itself withdrawn must also remove it from their Google account
permissions page.

There is no Microsoft OneDrive equivalent of this operation.

drive_id.description: Identifier of the stored connection, from the status listing.

get.summary: List files in a connected Google Drive
get.description:
Lists files visible to one connected Google Drive account.

`email` selects which connected account to read and is effectively required — the lookup
matches on it, so omitting it when several accounts are connected will not find a
credential and the call reports "not found or authorized" rather than defaulting to one.

Results are page-token based: pass the token returned by the previous call to continue.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Which connected account to read. Required when more than one is connected.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Files per page. Defaults to 100.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Continuation token from the previous page.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Provider-side search expression.

parameters.name: mime_type
parameters.description: MIME type filter. Accepts a single value or a comma-separated list.

200.description: Page of files plus the continuation token, when more remain.

post.summary: Download a Drive file, optionally storing it in Ambivo
post.description:
Fetches one file from a connected Google Drive.

The response shape depends on what you ask for. By default the file content is returned.
Set `create_file` to store it as an Ambivo file instead, and `get_url` to receive a link
rather than bytes. Supplying `kb_name` additionally indexes the stored file into that
knowledge base, which is the path used when populating a KB from Drive.

Native Google formats (Docs, Sheets, Slides) have no direct byte representation and must
be converted on the way out — set `export_mime_type` to choose the target format.
Omitting it for a native file is the usual cause of an empty or rejected download.

email.description: Which connected account holds the file.

export_mime_type.description: Target format for native Google formats. Required for Docs/Sheets/Slides.

create_file.description: Store the result as an Ambivo file rather than returning content.

display_name.description: Name for the stored file. Defaults to the Drive name.

folder_id.description: Destination Ambivo folder when `create_file` is set.

get_url.description: Return a link instead of the file content.

post.summary: Force a Google Drive access-token refresh
post.description:
Exchanges the stored refresh token for a fresh access token immediately.

Callers do not normally need this — the file and download endpoints refresh on demand.
It exists to let a client confirm a connection is still good, and to clear
`reauthorization_needed` after a user has re-consented.

A failure here means the grant is dead provider-side and the account must be reconnected
through the consent URL.

get.summary: Build the Microsoft OneDrive consent URL
get.description:
Microsoft OneDrive equivalent of `GET /gdrive/auth/url`, with identical semantics and
parameters. Returns the Microsoft consent URL; nothing is stored until the callback.

Consent is requested with `prompt=consent` so that a refresh token is reliably issued
rather than omitted on repeat authorizations.

parameters.name: post_navigation
parameters.description: Where to send the browser immediately after a successful callback.

parameters.name: final_navigation
parameters.description: Final destination once post-connect setup finishes.

get.summary: OAuth callback — exchanges the authorization code
get.description:
**Called by Microsoft, not by your application**, and unauthenticated for the same reason
as the Google callback: the provider redirects the browser here with no Bearer token.

Exchanges the code for tokens server to server and stores the refresh token against the
user and tenant named in `state`. Register this path as a redirect URI in the Microsoft
app registration.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Short-lived authorization code issued by Microsoft.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque value round-tripped from the authorization request.

200.description: Envelope reporting whether the connection was stored.

get.description:
Lists every OneDrive account the caller has connected in this tenant, with the same
shape as the Google listing.

Note the asymmetry with Google Drive: there is no DELETE on this path, so a OneDrive
connection cannot be removed through the API.

200.description: Connected drives, each with its live reauthorization state.

get.summary: List files in a connected OneDrive
get.description:
OneDrive equivalent of `GET /gdrive/files`, with the same parameters and paging model.
`email` selects which connected account to read.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Which connected account to read. Required when more than one is connected.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Files per page. Defaults to 100.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Continuation token from the previous page.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Provider-side search expression.

parameters.name: mime_type
parameters.description: MIME type filter. Accepts a single value or a comma-separated list.

200.description: Page of files plus the continuation token, when more remain.

post.summary: Download a OneDrive file, optionally storing it in Ambivo
post.description:
OneDrive equivalent of `POST /gdrive/download`, accepting the same body. `create_file`,
`get_url` and `kb_name` behave identically.

`export_mime_type` matters less here than on Google Drive, since Office documents already
have a byte representation and do not require conversion on export.

export_mime_type.description: Target format, when a conversion is wanted.

PaypalWebhookEvent.description:
Enriched PayPal event stored in MongoDB. Supports both Webhooks API (JSON)
and IPN (form-urlencoded) events. IPN events have `ambivo_source: "ipn"` and
synthesized `event_type` (e.g. `IPN.PAYMENT.COMPLETED`).

id.description: PayPal event ID (Webhooks API) or txn_id (IPN)

event_type.description:
PayPal event type (Webhooks API) or synthesized IPN type.
IPN types: `IPN.PAYMENT.COMPLETED`, `IPN.PAYMENT.REFUNDED`, `IPN.PAYMENT.PENDING`, etc.

resource.description: Event resource data (Webhooks API only — absent for IPN)

ambivo_sig_verified.description: Whether PayPal webhook signature was verified (true if skipped or verified, false if failed)

ambivo_source.description: 'ipn' for IPN events, absent for Webhooks API events
